observations: Photo 0: Used automatic transmission/gearbox unit, heavily soiled with grease and dirt, visible wiring harness and solenoid connectors.
Photo 1: Close-up of wiring harness, connector plugs, and starter motor area; wires appear loose/cut on one connector.
Photo 2: Side view of the same gearbox showing bellhousing, torque converter opening, and mounting bolts; blue paint marking visible on casing.
A watermark 'GOD OF ABRAHAM INVESTMENT' overlays all images; no manufacturer plate, part number, or VIN tag is legible in any shot.
No vehicle, engine, or fitment label is readable to confirm make/model compatibility.

claims.claim: Dealer in all kinds of Japanese parts and gearbox
claims.evidence: No shop signage, business registration, or vehicle fitment data shown in any photo.

claims.claim: Implied it is a functional, Japanese-make gearbox
claims.evidence: No maker's plate or part number visible in photo 0, 1, or 2 to confirm make; no test clip showing it turns or shifts.

risks.risk: Internal mechanical condition (gears, clutches, torque converter) unknown; could be seized, worn, or stripped internally
risks.proof: Video clip of input/output shaft being rotated by hand and torque converter spinning freely
risks.if_unproven: priced as not working / for parts

risks.risk: Loose or cut wiring near connector in photo 1 suggests possible sensor or solenoid damage
risks.proof: Close-up photo of the cut wire area and confirmation it is not an active sensor line
risks.if_unproven: priced as having electrical fault, deduct for repair

risks.risk: Exact vehicle make/model/engine fitment unverified, affects whether it matches buyer's car
risks.proof: Photo of embossed part number or manufacturer tag on casing
risks.if_unproven: priced as generic unverified-fitment unit, not model-specific

risks.risk: Fluid leaks or seal damage not assessable from dry, dirty casing
risks.proof: Photo of casing after wipe-down showing seals and any oil seepage

proof_requests: Clear photo of the manufacturer's part/serial plate on the gearbox casing
Video of the gearbox's input shaft/torque converter being rotated to show it is not seized
Close-up of the cut/loose wiring harness near the solenoid connector
Confirmation of which vehicle make/model/year this gearbox fits
response.reason: The item is a clearly identifiable used automatic transmission/gearbox by type, but with no legible part number, no functional test shown, and visible wiring damage, so it must be priced at worst case as an untested, possibly faulty unit pending the listed proofs.
